parts.title: A Brief History Of Canned Food
parts.article:
(A) In 1795, the French government had a problem: they faced the fact that it is not easy to win battles abroad when your soldiers are hungry and malnourished. That year they established a 12,000-franc prize for whoever could find a way to preserve food – from milk and meat to fruits and vegetables. French chef Nicolas Appert took more than a decade to develop a process that involved cooking food in glass jars and then using seals made of cork to make them airtight. In 1810, he published a book whose title translates as “The art of preserving all animal and vegetable substances for several years”, and collected his prize money. Appert’s achievement didn’t escape the notice of British merchant and inventor Peter Durand, who applied for a British patent later that year. Durand used techniques similar to Appert’s, although he adapted the model to include the use of tin vessels as well as glass jars.

(B) Following these discoveries, canned food was initially produced for soldiers and explorers. But even after people became aware of the existence of bacteria in the late 19th century, canning companies couldn’t work out exactly why some of their tins turned bad. And even into the 20th century, newspapers were full of accounts not only of food poisoning but also of cases of the fatal disease botulism resulting from people eating canned food. For that reason, many continued to look upon canned food with suspicion and fear.

(C) The US food manufacturer, The Heinz Company, realized bad cans were bad for business. From the 1890s to 1920s, the company insisted on weekly manicures for its canning-factory workers to ensure that any bacteria beneath employees’ fingernails stayed out of the food. Heinz employees were required to shower and change their clothing regularly. In an era when food-factory hygiene was not universally adopted, what might have been considered a nuisance by workers was at least good for consumers.

(D) Some canning companies killed bacteria with chemical additives such as sodium benzoate, which is still used today in canned food, and formaldehydes, which are now known to cause cancer. Some of the larger canning companies, such as Heinz, Libby, and Campbell’s, installed expensive steam-retort technology developed in the 1870s. Steam retorts worked like steam engines, using pressure to raise canning temperatures high enough to make food safe. Yet some batches of cans, even when made with this advanced technique, would explode after months on the shelf, while the contents of other cans might mysteriously sour. Smaller canning manufacturers relied on the open kettle method* and they had even less consistent results.

(E) US canning companies eventually banded together to discover the scientific principles affecting the canning process. In 1913, they launched the Research Laboratory of the National Canners Association in order to look into the elusive bacteriology responsible for all manner of spoiled canned food. The research done by the laboratory in the decades that followed helped resolve the problem of spoiled food and led to improved flavor, color, nutritional value, and texture.

(F) Before this time, canning companies had discovered through trial and error that the best way to avoid bad cans was to cook food at high temperatures for long periods, an approach that sacrificed flavor. “Food safety and palatability were often at cross-purposes,” remarks food historian Gabriella Petrick. For string beans, for instance, long cooking times in hot water leach out the green color, creating an unattractive grayish-toned bean. The addition of salt was one technique employed in the early 20th century to prevent this happening, thereby maintaining the visual appeal of the product and restoring a certain amount of taste.

(G) One of the major canning innovations of the 20th century was the development of aseptic processing. This technique, which involves sterilizing the container separately from the food, was invented in Switzerland in the 1960s for processing milk, but is now used widely for canned tomatoes and many juices. Small volumes of food are heated to a precise temperature and for a precise time in order to avoid overcooking and preserve color and nutrients, explains food scientist Philip Nelson, who won the 2007 World Food Prize in recognition of his research on making aseptic processing workable on a large industrial scale.

(H) Today, despite all the modern alternatives, Appert’s technology still reigns supreme for long-term storage. More than two centuries on, the simple can is still the best solution for the safe and effective preservation of a wide range of foodstuffs worldwide.

*open kettle method: food is cooked in a covered container and then poured while hot into sterile jars.

reference:
Q1

解析 原文提到1795年法国政府面临的问题是前线士兵（soldiers）挨饿，对应题目中的为国家提供食物。

干扰 你可能想填people，但原文明确指出了挨饿受冻的具体对象是打仗的士兵（soldiers）。

句子 In 1795, the French government had a problem: they faced the fact that it is not easy to win battles abroad when your soldiers are hungry and malnourished.

Q2

解析 原文提到Appert把食物放在玻璃罐里煮，然后用由软木塞（cork）制成的密封件来让它不透气，直接对应题目中“using（使用）”的内容。

干扰 你可能想填seals，但题目要填具体的材料，而原文说的是由软木（cork）制成的密封件。

句子 French chef Nicolas Appert took more than a decade to develop a process that involved cooking food in glass jars and then using seals made of cork to make them airtight. In 1810, he published a book whose title translates as “The art of preserving all animal and vegetable substances for several years”, and collected his prize money.

Q3

解析 原文明确说到Durand改进了模型，除了玻璃罐还使用了锡（tin）制的容器，对应题目的“containers made of...（由...制成的容器）”。

干扰 你可能想填vessels，但vessels其实就是题目里containers的同义词，这里需要填的是修饰容器的材质（tin）。

句子 Appert’s achievement didn’t escape the notice of British merchant and inventor Peter Durand, who applied for a British patent later that year. Durand used techniques similar to Appert’s, although he adapted the model to include the use of tin vessels as well as glass jars.

Q4

解析 原文指出蒸汽杀菌锅利用压力（pressure）来提高罐头加工的温度，完美对应题目中的“helps achieve high temperature（帮助达到高温）”。

干扰 你可能会去找某种燃料或机器部件，但原文直接点明了是利用“pressure（压力）”这一物理条件来提升温度的。

句子 Some of the larger canning companies, such as Heinz, Libby, and Campbell’s, installed expensive steam-retort technology developed in the 1870s. Steam retorts worked like steam engines, using pressure to raise canning temperatures high enough to make food safe.

Q5

解析 原文提到亨氏公司坚持给员工修指甲，是为了确保指甲里的细菌（bacteria）不进入食物，完全对应题目中的“reduce risk of... entering the product”。

干扰 你可能想填dirt或者其他污渍，但原文精确指出的防范对象是员工指甲里的细菌（bacteria）。

句子 The US food manufacturer, The Heinz Company, realized bad cans were bad for business. From the 1890s to 1920s, the company insisted on weekly manicures for its canning-factory workers to ensure that any bacteria beneath employees’ fingernails stayed out of the food.

Q6

解析 原文写的是成立“实验室”（Research Laboratory）去研究细菌学，所以填入 reasearch 形成 “organization for the purpose of research” 对应原文。

干扰 原文里 Research 是名词修饰 Laboratory，在题干中依然是名词，是没问题的。

句子 US canning companies eventually banded together to discover the scientific principles affecting the canning process. In 1913, they launched the Research Laboratory of the National Canners Association in order to look into the elusive bacteriology responsible for all manner of spoiled canned food. The research done by the laboratory in the decades that followed helped resolve the problem of spoiled food and led to improved flavor, color, nutritional value, and texture.

Q7

解析 原文提到这种在60年代发明的无菌处理技术最初是用来处理牛奶（milk）的，后来才被广泛应用到现在的罐头加工上。

干扰 你可能想填tomatoes或juices，但这些是后来应用的对象，题目问的是这项技术最初开发是为了和什么（milk）一起使用的。

句子 One of the major canning innovations of the 20th century was the development of aseptic processing. This technique, which involves sterilizing the container separately from the food, was invented in Switzerland in the 1960s for processing milk, but is now used widely for canned tomatoes and many juices.

Q8

解析 原文提到20世纪初采用添加盐（salt）的技术来防止豆子在热水中长时间煮而褪色，对应题目中的“avoid loss of colour during cooking process”。

干扰 你可能看到color就想填green，但题目问的是“什么被用来（was used）”防止褪色，原文指出的动作主语是“The addition of salt（加盐）”。

句子 For string beans, for instance, long cooking times in hot water leach out the green color, creating an unattractive grayish-toned bean. The addition of salt was one technique employed in the early 20th century to prevent this happening, thereby maintaining the visual appeal of the product and restoring a certain amount of taste.

Q9

解析 原文说到Durand使用的技术与Appert类似，而上文刚说到Appert正是因为这个方法赢得了奖金，题目表述与原文的逻辑链完全一致。

干扰 你可能会因为原文没把“Durand”和“prize”写在同一个句子里而选NOT GIVEN，但跨句联系上下文可知，Durand模仿的正是刚拿奖的技术。

句子 In 1810, he published a book whose title translates as “The art of preserving all animal and vegetable substances for several years”, and collected his prize money. Appert’s achievement didn’t escape the notice of British merchant and inventor Peter Durand, who applied for a British patent later that year. Durand used techniques similar to Appert’s...

Q10

解析 原文明确交代早期的罐头食品最初是为士兵和探险家（soldiers and explorers）生产的，与题目中针对大众（general public）的说法直接相悖。

干扰 你可能会凭生活常识觉得罐头就是给普通大众吃的而错选TRUE，但在雅思阅读中必须百分之百忠于原文信息。

句子 Following these discoveries, canned food was initially produced for soldiers and explorers.

Q11

解析 原文虽然提到了罐头公司不知道变坏的原因，也提到了报纸上到处都是食物中毒的报道，但压根没有提到生产商是否“拒绝承担责任（denied responsibility）”。

干扰 你可能会脑补生产商因为查不出原因就推卸责任而错选TRUE，但记住“没写就是没写”，千万不要自己根据情景加戏。

句子 But even after people became aware of the existence of bacteria in the late 19th century, canning companies couldn’t work out exactly why some of their tins turned bad. And even into the 20th century, newspapers were full of accounts not only of food poisoning but also of cases of the fatal disease botulism resulting from people eating canned food.

Q12

解析 原文只说明了亨氏公司对员工的卫生规定对消费者有好处（good for consumers），但完全没提及这是否导致了“产品销量增加（increase in sales）”。

干扰 你可能会理所当然地把“对消费者好”等同于“销量一定会增加”从而错选TRUE，但这种商业结果在原文中并没有任何事实依据。

句子 The US food manufacturer, The Heinz Company, realized bad cans were bad for business. From the 1890s to 1920s, the company insisted on weekly manicures for its canning-factory workers... ...what might have been considered a nuisance by workers was at least good for consumers.

Q13

解析 原文明确指出某些化学添加剂（如苯甲酸钠）“至今仍在使用（still used today）”，直接推翻了题目中“被放弃使用（abandoned）”的说法。

干扰 你可能会因为后面紧接着介绍了新式蒸汽技术，就以为旧的化学方法已经被淘汰了，但一定要盯紧并相信“still used today”这个关键细节。

句子 Some canning companies killed bacteria with chemical additives such as sodium benzoate, which is still used today in canned food, and formaldehydes, which are now known to cause cancer. Some of the larger canning companies, such as Heinz, Libby, and Campbell’s, installed expensive steam-retort technology developed in the 1870s.
